raw_response:
I've farmed this land my whole life. My fields are on the flat plain just like everyone else around here. Five mu total — that's what my family has. I don't need to think hard about what to grow. My mother grew wheat and corn, my neighbors grow wheat and corn, and I will too. That's what this land is for. After the wheat comes off in June, the corn goes in right away on the same ground. That's how we do it here.

For seeds I go to the seed station in town. The man there tells me what's been working well this year. I don't bother with the old varieties my grandmother used — the new wheat seeds give a bigger harvest and stand up better when there's wind. For corn I always buy the hybrid bags. They cost more but the yield is worth it.

Fertilizer — I put down the compound fertilizer before planting, then I add urea in spring when the wheat is growing tall. I put a decent amount. You can't be stingy with fertilizer if you want a real harvest.

For water, wheat needs more attention than corn. I run the pump four times for wheat — once before seeding to wet the soil, once before the cold sets in, once when it's jointing in spring, and once more when heads form. Corn mostly gets the summer rain but if it's dry in July I'll water it once.

Near the house I have half a mu of vegetables — cabbage, garlic, beans, some peppers. That's for us to eat. I don't sell it.
